title: The psychology behind our political divide, with Keith Payne, PhD

sentences.en: If you listen to the news or to political pundits, you've probably heard that Americans are more politically polarized than ever before.
sentences.zh: 如果你经常看新闻或政论节目，你可能听说过，现在的美国人比以往任何时候都更加政治对立。

sentences.en: We've sorted ourselves into opposing red and blue camps, and we can't seem to see eye to eye on anything.
sentences.zh: 我们分化成了相互对立的红蓝两大阵营，而且在任何事情上似乎都无法达成共识。

sentences.en: With election day around the corner, many of us are feeling the strain of those divisions.
sentences.zh: 随着大选日日益临近，我们许多人都感受到了这种分歧带来的压力。

sentences.en: When you're getting into an angry debate with a childhood friend on Facebook or biting your tongue at a family dinner to keep the peace, the political divide can feel unbridgeable.
sentences.zh: 每当你与童年好友在脸书上陷入激烈的争论，或者在家庭聚会上为了维持和平而欲言又止时，这种政治鸿沟就会让人感到难以逾越。

sentences.en: Amid that strain, psychologist research can offer some insight.
sentences.zh: 在这种压力之下，心理学研究或许能提供一些深刻的见解。

sentences.en: It can help us understand where our political identities come from, why we think about politics the way we do, and why it's so hard to talk across the political divide.
sentences.zh: 它能帮助我们理解我们的政治身份从何而来，为什么我们对政治持有目前的看法，以及为什么跨越政治鸿沟的对话如此艰难。

sentences.en: So what is the psychology that underlies how most people think about politics?
sentences.zh: 那么，大多数人看待政治的方式背后，究竟蕴含着怎样的心理学？

sentences.en: How did American history and our own places in it lead each of us where we are?
sentences.zh: 美国历史以及我们在其中的位置，是如何把我们每个人带到今天这一步的？

sentences.en: Is the political divide today really worse than it was years ago?
sentences.zh: 如今的政治分歧真的比多年前更严重吗？

sentences.en: Does social media cause political polarization or does it just reflect it?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体是导致政治对立的罪魁祸首，还是仅仅折射了这种对立？

sentences.en: And what can we do to bridge the divide and maintain connections with those we disagree with?
sentences.zh: 我们究竟能做些什么来弥合分歧，并与那些意见不合的人保持联系？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是

sentences.en: Dr. Keith Payne, a professor of psychology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
sentences.zh: 基思·佩恩博士，他是北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的心理学教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Payne is a social psychologist who studies inequality and political polarization.
sentences.zh: 佩恩博士是一位研究不平等和政治对立的社会心理学家。

sentences.en: His work has been featured in the New York Times and the Atlantic and on NPR.
sentences.zh: 他的作品曾被《纽约时报》、《大西洋月刊》以及全国公共广播电台报道。

sentences.en: He's author of the 2017 book,
sentences.zh: 他是2017年出版的以下书籍的作者：

sentences.en: The Broken Ladder, How Inequality Affects the Way We Live, Think, and Die.
sentences.zh: 《破梯：不平等如何影响我们的生活、思维与死亡》。

sentences.en: His new book coming out in
sentences.zh: 他将于

sentences.en: October is called Good Reasonable People, The Psychology Behind America's Dangerous Divide.
sentences.zh: 10月出版的新书名为《善良理性的人：美国危险分歧背后的心理学》。

sentences.en: Dr. Payne, starts with a very personal note.
sentences.zh: 佩恩博士，让我们从一个非常私人的话题开始。

sentences.en: It opens with stories about your childhood in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 这本书以你在肯塔基州度过的童年故事开篇。

sentences.en: Can you tell us a little bit about your background and how it led to your interest in polarization?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们聊聊你的背景，以及它是如何让你对政治对立产生兴趣的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I grew up in a small town in western Kentucky, a town called Maceo that has about 400
sentences.zh: 好的，我是在西肯塔基州的一个小镇长大的，那个镇叫马塞奥，大约有400

sentences.en: people that is, I believe, as of recent census count still 100% white and has very little diversity when I was growing up, overwhelmingly conservative, white, and Christian.
sentences.zh: 人。根据最近的人口普查，据我所知，那里仍然是100%的白人。在我成长的时候，那里几乎没有什么多元化，绝大多数都是保守派、白人和基督徒。

sentences.en: And the kinds of dynamics that I saw growing up within my family during, especially starting around the 1990s, where some people
sentences.zh: 我在成长过程中看到家人身上出现了一些动态变化，特别是从20世纪90年代开始，有些人

sentences.en: started to pull away from the way that other people in my community tended to think.
sentences.zh: 开始与我社区里其他人习惯的思维方式渐行渐远。

sentences.en: I thought that was just something that was happening in my family, something that was happening in my little town.
sentences.zh: 我以前以为这只是发生在我家里的事情，只是发生在我这个小镇上的事情。

sentences.en: And it turned out over time, I started to realize that those were the same kinds of divides that were happening across the country as a whole.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，我开始意识到，这些正是整个国家正在发生的那类分歧。

sentences.en: So people were sorting themselves more and more based on factors like race and religion and education.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们越来越多地根据种族、宗教和教育等因素对自身进行归类划分。

sentences.en: And I started to see those cleavages happening within my own family.
sentences.zh: 我开始看到这种撕裂在我的大家庭内部发生。

sentences.en: And as polarization became more and more intense and emotional and widespread over the last
sentences.zh: 随着过去

sentences.en: 20 or 30 years, I've been drawn to look more and more closely at the psychology of it and what's happening at a broader level.
sentences.zh: 二三十年里，政治对立变得越来越激烈、充满情绪化且广泛蔓延，我被吸引去更仔细地审视其背后的心理机制以及更广泛层面上正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: There's a quote in your new book that struck me, which is, there is no liberal mind or conservative mind.
sentences.zh: 你的新书里有一句话让我感触颇深，那就是：没有所谓的自由派大脑或保守派大脑。

sentences.en: There are only human minds trying to make sense of the circumstances in which they find themselves.
sentences.zh: 只有人类的大脑在试图理解他们所处的环境。

sentences.en: That idea goes against what I think many of us believe, which is that there are real differences between liberals and conservatives in terms of personality or other attributes.
sentences.zh: 这个观点违背了我认为我们许多人的信仰，即自由派和保守派在个性或其他属性方面存在真正的差异。

sentences.en: Can you explain what you meant by that and what the research is behind that statement?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下你这话是什么意思，以及该陈述背后的研究是什么吗？

sentences.en: There's definitely differences between liberals and conservatives or Democrats and Republicans in terms of what they think, the content of their beliefs and their attitudes.
sentences.zh: 自由派和保守派，或者民主党人和共和党人，在他们的想法、信念和态度的内容上确实存在差异。

sentences.en: But in terms of the basic psychology behind how we make sense of politics, how we make sense of our social worlds more broadly, we are all working with the same hardware, right?
sentences.zh: 但就我们如何理解政治、如何更广泛地理解社会世界的底层心理学而言，我们大家使用的都是同一套硬件，对吧？

sentences.en: We've all got the same kinds of minds.
sentences.zh: 我们都有着同类的大脑。

sentences.en: And what we're doing is we're living in different circumstances, different social worlds, different geographies often.
sentences.zh: 我们在做的是，生活在不同的环境中，不同的社会世界里，通常还有不同的地理位置。

sentences.en: And what we're all doing is trying to make sense of that world from the perspective of the social groups and the contexts that we belong to.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都在做的事情，就是试图从我们所属的社会群体和背景的角度去理解这个世界。

sentences.en: So there is a lot of research about the relationship between personality and political differences.
sentences.zh: 因此，有大量关于个性与政治差异之间关系的研究。

sentences.en: And there are some personality differences between Democrats and Republicans on average.
sentences.zh: 就平均水平而言，民主党人和共和党人之间确实存在一些个性差异。

sentences.en: For example, Democrats or liberals tend to be higher in a trait called openness to experience.
sentences.zh: 例如，民主党人或自由派在一种名为“开放性体验”的特质上往往得分更高。

sentences.en: There are a few other personality traits that consistently correlate with political differences.
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些个性特质与政治差异持续相关。

sentences.en: But the thing to keep in mind is those differences are quite small.
sentences.zh: 但需要记住的是，这些差异相当小。

sentences.en: They're not zero.
sentences.zh: 它们不是零。

sentences.en: They're real.
sentences.zh: 它们是真实的。

sentences.en: But it amounts to showing that Democrats are a few percentage points higher on a trait like openness to experience than Republicans.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，它表明民主党人在开放性体验这样的特质上只比共和党人高出几个百分点。

sentences.en: Republicans might be a few percentage points higher on traits like the need for structure or need to think about things in a clear, structured way.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在对结构的需求或以清晰、结构化方式思考事物的需求等特质上，可能会高出几个百分点。

sentences.en: But those few percentage points that separate liberals and conservatives on those personality dimensions don't go anywhere close to explaining the giant gulfs we see between people
sentences.zh: 但是，在这些个性维度上将自由派和保守派区分开来的那几个百分点，根本无法用来解释我们在人们之间看到的巨大鸿沟——

sentences.en: people based on their social groups, based on social identities, which are often tied to these demographic differences.
sentences.zh: 人们基于他们的社会群体、基于社会认同而产生的鸿沟，而这些认同通常与这些人口统计学差异息息相关。

sentences.en: Now, you make the point in the book that people think that political polarization is about policy disagreements and different philosophies.
sentences.zh: 你在书中指出，人们认为政治对立是关于政策分歧和不同哲学观点的。

sentences.en: But really, as you were just saying, they're about identity.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，正如你刚才所说，它们关乎身份认同。

sentences.en: Can you elaborate on that more?
sentences.zh: 你能对此作更详细的阐述吗？

sentences.en: When we talk about political ideology, what we're talking about is a coherent set of political principles, or at least an interrelated set of values and issue stands.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论政治意识形态时，我们讨论的是一套连贯的政治原则，或者至少是一套相互关联的价值观和议题立场。

sentences.en: That's what we mean when I say that somebody has a liberal ideology or a conservative ideology.
sentences.zh: 这就是当我讲某人拥有自由派意识形态或保守派意识形态时我们的意思。

sentences.en: But social scientists have known since at least the 1960s, that if you look at the actual views of the American public, they don't tend to fall
sentences.zh: 但社会科学家至少从20世纪60年代就已经知道，如果你审视美国公众的实际观点，你会发现它们并不倾向于

sentences.en: along any consistent ideological lines when it comes to issues and political principles.
sentences.zh: 在涉及议题和政治原则时顺应任何一致的意识形态路线。

sentences.en: So if you look at somebody's attitude toward one issue, like tax cuts or tax increases, and you look at their attitudes
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你看看某人对某个议题的态度，比如减税或增税，再看看他们对其他议题的态度

sentences.en: toward other issues like government spending or government budget cuts, you would think that logically those two things would be connected to each other.
sentences.zh: ——比如政府开支或政府预算削减，你可能会从逻辑上认为这两者是彼此相连的。

sentences.en: But they're actually very weakly correlated with each other when we look at real people's polling or survey data.
sentences.zh: 但当我们查看真实人群的民调或调查数据时，它们之间的相关性实际上非常微弱。

sentences.en: And if you look at the same person's responses over time, if you ask them the exact same question about a policy issue or a political principle, they often
sentences.zh: 如果你观察同一个人在不同时期的回答，如果你向他们提出关于政策议题或政治原则的完全相同的问题，他们往往

sentences.en: give you a very different response six months or a year later.
sentences.zh: 会在六个月或一年后给出截然不同的回答。

sentences.en: So they don't even agree with themselves very well.
sentences.zh: 所以他们甚至连自己都无法很好地赞同。

sentences.en: And political scientists have estimated that if you think of an ideology as a coherent and stable
sentences.zh: 政治科学家估计，如果你把意识形态看作是一套连贯、稳定且

sentences.en: interconnected set of ideas, only about 15% of the American public has what would qualify as an ideology in that sense.
sentences.zh: 相互关联的思想体系，那么美国公众中只有大约15%的人具备这种意义上的意识形态。

sentences.en: The vast majority of us, about 85%, don't have what we would really consider an ideology.
sentences.zh: 我们绝大多数人，大约85%，并不具备我们真正认为的意识形态。

sentences.en: What we have instead is a social identity.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们拥有的是社会认同。

sentences.en: We know who our people are.
sentences.zh: 我们知道谁是我们的同类。

sentences.en: We might identify strongly with one political party or the other, and we might really dislike the other group.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会强烈认同某个政党，并且可能会非常厌恶另一个群体。

sentences.en: But those sentiments are tied much more closely to our social group identities than to anything about policy or political philosophy.
sentences.zh: 但这些情绪与我们的社会群体认同的联系，远大于与政策或政治哲学的任何关系的联系。

sentences.en: And all of this would seem to add up to the fact that political polling is very imprecise, right?
sentences.zh: 所有这一切似乎都表明，政治民意调查非常不精确，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, people will answer the same question differently on a different day of the week.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们在星期的不同日子里对同一个问题会有不同的回答。

sentences.en: Yeah, it could be that polling is imprecise, but I think probably more than that, at least polling, we can quantify how imprecise it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，民调可能不精确，但我认为比这更甚的是，至少在民调方面，我们可以量化它有多不精确。

sentences.en: We have a margin of error.
sentences.zh: 我们有误差范围。

sentences.en: And so we can estimate how off we are likely to be.
sentences.zh: 因此我们可以估计我们的偏差可能有多大。

sentences.en: The thing is, I think when people are inconsistent over time, it's usually because they're giving us the best answer they have at time one.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我认为当人们的观点随时间推移而前后不一时，通常是因为他们在时间点一时给出了他们当时能给出的最佳答案。

sentences.en: And then when we recontact them a year later, they're giving us the best answer they have at time two.
sentences.zh: 然后，当我们一年后再次联系他们时，他们给出的是在时间点二时他们拥有的最佳答案。

sentences.en: And those aren't always very stable.
sentences.zh: 而这些并不总是那么稳定。

sentences.en: I think a lot of it comes down to the fact that those of us who are reading and writing and talking
sentences.zh: 我认为很大程度上归结于这样一个事实：我们这些整天在阅读、写作和谈论

sentences.en: about politics all the time assume that everybody else is a political junkie like us.
sentences.zh: 政治的人，总是假设其他所有人都跟我们一样是个政治迷。

sentences.en: So the so-called elites like journalists and academics and political leaders themselves, we eat and sleep and breathe this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以所谓的精英，比如记者、学者和政治领袖本身，我们满脑子想的都是这些东西。

sentences.en: And we assume that other people do as well.
sentences.zh: 并且我们假设其他人也是如此。

sentences.en: But that's just not true.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: It's not that central or meaningful in the daily lives of most people.
sentences.zh: 它在大多数人的日常生活中并没有那么核心或意义重大。

sentences.en: And so imagine if you call people up and just assume that they had detailed opinions about classical music or something that's esoteric to most ordinary
sentences.zh: 因此，想象一下，如果你打电话给人们，只是假设他们对古典音乐或某些对大多数普通人来说

sentences.en: people, and you ask them detailed questions about their preferences and attitudes in the area of classical music.
sentences.zh: 属于深奥的事物有详细的看法，并向他们询问有关古典音乐领域的偏好和态度的详细问题。

sentences.en: A lot of times people would give you an answer, but it might not mean anything.
sentences.zh: 很多时候人们会给你一个答案，但这可能没有任何意义。

sentences.en: It might just be what they're thinking at the moment.
sentences.zh: 这可能只是他们当时的临时想法。

sentences.en: And then if you call them up a year later and ask them a question again, they're probably not going to have a consistent opinion on that
sentences.zh: 然后，如果你一年后打电话给他们，再次向他们提问，他们可能不会对那个问题保持一致的看法

sentences.en: because it's not something they spend their time thinking about.
sentences.zh: 因为这不是他们花时间去思考的事情。

sentences.en: In your new book, you also talk about what you're calling the psychological immune system and how we use it to validate what we already believe.
sentences.zh: 在你的新书中，你还谈到了你所谓的心理免疫系统，以及我们如何用它来佐证我们原有的信仰。

sentences.en: And you also talk about something called motivated reasoning.
sentences.zh: 你还谈到了一种叫做动机性推理的机制。

sentences.en: So can you talk about those two concepts, how they're different, how they're the same, and how we use them?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能谈谈这两个概念、它们的区别与联系，以及我们是如何运用它们的吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So motivated reasoning is the idea that whenever we're thinking and reasoning, we're not just reasoning for the purpose of finding truth.
sentences.zh: 所以，动机性推理指的是这样一个概念：每当我们思考和推理时，我们的目的并不仅仅是为了寻找真相。

sentences.en: That's one thing we're trying to do.
sentences.zh: 那是我们试图做的事情之一。

sentences.en: We're trying to find true answers about the world.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图找到关于世界的真实答案。

sentences.en: But another thing we're trying to do at the same time is to reassure ourselves that we're good and reasonable people.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们试图做的另一件事是让自己确信我们是善良和理性的人。

sentences.en: And that's where the name for the book comes from.
sentences.zh: 这也是书名的由来。

sentences.en: So a lot of the thinking we do is aimed at reassuring ourselves that we're good members of our social group, that we're good and reasonable people, and the people in our groups
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的许多思考都旨在让自己确信我们是社会群体中的优秀成员，我们是善良和理性的人，并且我们群体中那些对我们意义重大的人

sentences.en: that mean a lot to us are as well.
sentences.zh: 也是如此。

sentences.en: So motivated reasoning is one of the main mechanisms that we deploy in what psychologists have called the psychological immune system.
sentences.zh: 因此，动机性推理是我们在心理学家所谓的“心理免疫系统”中所调动的主要机制之一。

sentences.en: The idea behind the psychological immune system is that we have a suite of psychological processes, thought processes,
sentences.zh: 心理免疫系统背后的理念是，我们拥有一套心理过程、思维过程，

sentences.en: that we use to defend our sense of self as a good and reasonable member of our groups, akin to the way that the biological immune system destroys biological threats to the body.
sentences.zh: 我们用它们来捍卫自我意识，将自己标榜为群体中善良且理性的成员，这类似于生物免疫系统摧毁对身体的生物威胁。

sentences.en: So the psychological immune system is similar to other ideas in psychology, like coping with stress or defense mechanisms from an older Freudian point of view.
sentences.zh: 所以，心理免疫系统类似于心理学中的其他概念，比如用较老弗洛伊德的观点来看应对压力或防御机制。

sentences.en: It's the ways that we go about coming up with interpretations of new information, rationalizations and justifications for whatever we do or say or think, to interpret all
sentences.zh: 这是我们用来对新信息做出诠释的方式，是我们为自己所做、所说或所想的一切进行合理化和辩解的方式，从而将所有这一切

sentences.en: of that in a way that adds up to this psychological bottom line that I'm a good and reasonable person.
sentences.zh: 解读为汇聚成这样一个心理底线：我是一个善良而理性的人。

sentences.en: And is that different from confirmation bias?
sentences.zh: 这与确认偏误不同吗？

sentences.en: Because as I was reading the book, I was thinking, you know, there's definitely a relationship going on here that people find information, they accept it,
sentences.zh: 因为当我在阅读这本书时，我在想，你知道，这里面绝对存在某种联系，人们寻找信息，接受它，

sentences.en: they ingest it, they believe it, because it comports with things that they were already thinking.
sentences.zh: 吸收它，相信它，是因为它符合他们原本就有的想法。

sentences.en: Confirmation bias is one of the tools we use, for sure.
sentences.zh: 确认偏误确实是我们使用的工具之一。

sentences.en: So confirmation bias is the tendency to look for or generate evidence that's consistent with ideas that we already believed are true.
sentences.zh: 因此，确认偏误是倾向于寻找或生成与我们原本认为正确的观点相一致的证据。

sentences.en: So that's definitely one tool that we use as part of the psychological immune system, as part of this idea of motivated reasoning.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是我们作为心理免疫系统的一部分、作为这种动机性推理理念的一部分所使用的工具。

sentences.en: But the psychological immune system is broader than that.
sentences.zh: 但心理免疫系统的范围比这更广泛。

sentences.en: Sometimes it can be confirmation bias that serves the goal of reassuring us that we're a good person.
sentences.zh: 有时它可能是为了服务于“确信我们是个好人”这一目标的确认偏误。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's changing our opinion and taking on the new opinion, maybe of a social group that means a lot to us, if that's what makes us feel like a good member of that group.
sentences.zh: 有时则是改变我们的意见并接受新的观点，比如某个对我们意义重大的社会群体的观点，如果这样做能让我们感觉自己是该群体的优秀成员的话。

sentences.en: I was just wondering, again, as I was reading, reading the book, whether you believe that it's actually possible to change other people's opinions?
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，同样地，当我在阅读这本书时，你是否认为改变别人的观点其实是可能的？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's possible for people's opinions to change.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为人们的观点是有可能改变的。

sentences.en: That's not the same thing as saying it's possible to change other people's opinions.
sentences.zh: 但这并不等于说改变别人的观点是可能的。

sentences.en: Psychologists talk about something called the cognitive response principle, which is the idea that anytime you present information or an argument
sentences.zh: 心理学家讨论过一个叫做“认知反应原则”的概念，其核心思想是：每当你向某人提供信息、论点

sentences.en: or a persuasive attempt to somebody to try to change what they believe, they never change in response to that external influence that you've tried to exert.
sentences.zh: 或说服尝试以试图改变他们的信仰时，他们从不会因为你试图施加的外部影响而直接改变。

sentences.en: If they change, it's because they've generated cognitive responses, thoughts of their own, that they then listen to and change based on their own inner thought processes.
sentences.zh: 如果他们发生了改变，那是因为他们产生了认知反应，即他们自己的想法，然后他们倾听这些想法，并根据他们自己内心的思维过程做出改变。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you try to change somebody's opinion and their internal monologue is, well, that's a crazy argument.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你试图改变某个人的观点，而他们的内心独白是：嗯，那真是一个荒谬的论点。

sentences.en: That doesn't make any sense at all.
sentences.zh: 那根本毫无道理。

sentences.en: Then your attempt is probably going to backfire because you presented them with arguments for X and their thoughts are that X is false.
sentences.zh: 那么你的尝试很可能会适得其反，因为你向他们提出了支持X的论点，而他们的想法是X是假的。

sentences.en: So, they're going to listen to their own thoughts.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们会倾听他们自己的想法。

sentences.en: And in that case, they're not going to change their opinion.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们是不会改变看法的。

sentences.en: Maybe they're even more opposed to your argument than they were before.
sentences.zh: 也许他们对你的论点的抵触情绪比以前更强烈了。

sentences.en: But if you're in a circumstance where you provide people with an argument or a persuasive attempt and their cognitive response to that is positive, then
sentences.zh: 但如果你所处的环境是，你向人们提供了一个论点或说服尝试，而他们对此的认知反应是积极的，那么

sentences.en: they might change their opinion based on their own thought processes.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会根据他们自己的思维过程改变自己的观点。

sentences.en: So, every time we try to change somebody else's opinion, we're just setting an occasion for them to generate their own arguments and listen to themselves.
sentences.zh: 因此，每当我们试图改变别人的观点时，我们只是在为他们提供一个契机，让他们去生成自己的论点并倾听他们自己。

sentences.en: You go back into the early history of the United States to explain many of our historical divisions.
sentences.zh: 你回溯到了美国早期的历史来解释我们的许多历史分歧。

sentences.en: How has that history contributed to the divisions we're seeing today?
sentences.zh: 这段历史是如何促成我们今天看到的分歧的？

sentences.en: So, when we look around us and try to make sense of the world, a lot depends on the arrangements and the systems and the group statuses that are in that environment around us.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们环顾四周并试图理解这个世界时，很大程度上取决于我们周围环境中的安排、系统和群体地位。

sentences.en: And those circumstances have been put into place by historical processes that started long before we were born.
sentences.zh: 而这些环境是由远在我们出生之前就开始的历史进程所确立的。

sentences.en: One of the factors that I look at in the book is the way that the United States Civil War and the
sentences.zh: 我在书中探讨的因素之一，是美国内战以及

sentences.en: Reconstruction period following the Civil War set up systems and structures related to racial inequality,
sentences.zh: 内战之后的重建时期是如何建立起与种族不平等相关的系统和结构的，

sentences.en: especially in the South, the resistance to racial equality during the Reconstruction period.
sentences.zh: 特别是在南方，重建时期对种族平等的抵抗。

sentences.en: So, you can look at census data on the number of people who were enslaved in each county on the eve of the Civil War in 1860.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以查阅人口普查数据，看看在1860年内战前夕，每个县被奴役的人口数量。

sentences.en: And political scientists have found that that is a good predictor of white Americans' political leanings today.
sentences.zh: 政治科学家发现，这是预测美国白人今天的政治倾向的一个很好的指标。

sentences.en: And the connection, in my view, is that those places that were more dependent on slavery in 1860 during the period following the Civil War set up systems that were
sentences.zh: 在我看来，其中的联系在于：那些在1860年更依赖奴隶制的地区，在内战之后的时期建立起来的系统

sentences.en: more unequal, more segregated by race, led to Jim Crow segregation for about a hundred years.
sentences.zh: 更加不平等，按种族隔离得更严重，导致了长达约一百年的吉姆·克劳种族隔离制度。

sentences.en: And those places are still more racially unequal today.
sentences.zh: 而这些地方今天在种族上仍然更加不平等。

sentences.en: And it's not just a broad north-south difference.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是广泛的南北差异。

sentences.en: You can look county to county and those places that had more slavery because the soil was more favorable to growing
sentences.zh: 你可以逐个县进行观察，那些奴隶较多的地方是因为土壤更适合种植

sentences.en: cotton versus the county next door that might have had a geography that didn't favor growing cotton.
sentences.zh: 棉花，而隔壁的县地理条件可能并不适合种植棉花。

sentences.en: You can see county to county differences today in the politics of the white and black residents in those counties.
sentences.zh: 你今天可以看到这些县的白人和黑人居民在政治上存在县与县之间的差异。

sentences.en: So, what seems to be happening is that people don't, on a general day-to-day basis, go around thinking about what was happening in 1860.
sentences.zh: 所以，目前的情况似乎是，人们在日常生活中并不会去思考1860年发生了什么。

sentences.en: What they do is look around them today.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的是看看他们今天的周围。

sentences.en: And in places that have a lot of racial inequality, the average white American tends to interpret that as something
sentences.zh: 而在许多存在种族不平等的地区，美国普通白人往往会将这种现象解释为

sentences.en: not about history and systems that have led to disadvantages for black Americans.
sentences.zh: 与导致美国黑人处于不利地位的历史和制度无关。

sentences.en: They tend to interpret that as something about current-day motivations and behaviors of white and black Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们往往将其解释为与美国白人和黑人当下的动机和行为有关。

sentences.en: So, white Americans today who live in a place that used to have a lot of slavery tend to think that racial inequality is due to black Americans not working as hard.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天生活在过去奴隶制盛行地区的美国白人，往往认为种族不平等是由于美国黑人工作不够努力造成的。

sentences.en: And that is highly correlated with Republican identity.
sentences.zh: 这与共和党人的身份认同高度相关。

sentences.en: Whereas in those same areas, those same counties with lots of racial inequality today,
sentences.zh: 而在这些相同的地区、这些今天存在大量种族不平等的相同县里，

sentences.en: black Americans tend to interpret that same racial inequality as something about the history and the systems of racial discrimination.
sentences.zh: 美国黑人往往将同样的种族不平等解释为与种族歧视的历史和制度有关。

sentences.en: And that is highly correlated with the Democratic identity.
sentences.zh: 这与民主党人的身份认同高度相关。

sentences.en: Jared So, given how polarized everything was at that point in our history, as we were talking about the
sentences.zh: 贾里d，鉴于我们历史上的那个节点一切都如此两极分化，正如我们一直在讨论的

sentences.en: Civil War and Reconstruction, are we more or less polarized today?
sentences.zh: 内战和重建时期，我们今天是更加两极分化还是不那么两极分化了？

sentences.en: Is there any way of knowing whether qualitatively or quantitatively it's different?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么办法能从定性或定量上知道它是否有所不同？

sentences.en: Jared Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 贾里d，嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: If we compare it to the Civil War, I would say we're probably at the most polarized in some ways than we have been since the Civil War and the aftermath.
sentences.zh: 如果与内战进行比较，我会说在某些方面，我们可能正处于自内战及其余波以来两极分化最严重的时期。

sentences.en: But whether we're more polarized today than we were, say, 30 or 40 years ago depends on whether we're talking about
sentences.zh: 但我们今天是否比比如说30或40年前更两极分化，取决于我们讨论的是

sentences.en: polarization in terms of issues versus polarization in terms of group identities and emotions.
sentences.zh: 基于议题的两极分化，还是基于群体认同和情绪的两极分化。

sentences.en: Because if you look at issue stands and policy preferences, Republicans and Democrats today aren't very far apart.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你看看立场和政策偏好，今天的共和党人和民主党人并没有相差太远。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if you look at how strongly people identify with their political groups and how much antagonism they feel toward the other side, that has really grown
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果你看看人们对自己的政治群体认同有多强烈，以及他们对另一方感到多少敌意，那确实在过去

sentences.en: over the last 30 or 40 years.
sentences.zh: 30或40年里增长了。

sentences.en: Jared Do you think that social media and partisan news channels are driving some of this polarization, or are they just reflecting the divisions that exist anyway?
sentences.zh: 贾里d，你认为社交媒体和党派新闻频道正在推动这种两极分化的一部分，还是它们只是反映了本就存在的裂痕？

sentences.en: Jared Well, one thing that social media and polarized news outlets do is magnify a division that's there and make it easy to communicate and spread that polarization.
sentences.zh: 贾里d，嗯，社交媒体和两极分化的新闻媒体所做的一件事，就是放大本就存在的裂痕，并使这种两极分化的沟通和传播变得容易。

sentences.en: But again, it depends on what exactly you mean by polarization here.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这取决于你这里所说的两极分化究竟是什么意思。

sentences.en: So social media is very good at spreading outrage.
sentences.zh: 所以社交媒体非常擅长传播愤怒。

sentences.en: And moral outrage in particular is something that makes a post more likely to go viral.
sentences.zh: 尤其是道德愤怒，它会让一则帖子更容易在网上病毒式传播。

sentences.en: So in that sense, social media is critical in the spread and possibly the growth of polarization.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，社交媒体对于两极分化的传播和可能的增长起到了关键作用。

sentences.en: But if you look at other metrics that are often blamed on social media, like the spread of misinformation and conspiracy theories, there the evidence is not so clear.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看其他常被归咎于社交媒体的指标，比如虚假信息和阴谋论的传播，那里的证据并不是那么明确。

sentences.en: I think the jury is still out on the role of social media in spreading that misinformation.
sentences.zh: 我认为社交媒体在传播这些虚假信息方面扮演的角色目前尚未有定论。

sentences.en: There's an interesting set of studies that recently came out looking at how Americans beliefs in misinformation and conspiracy theories has
sentences.zh: 最近有一系列有趣的研究出炉，探讨了美国人对阴谋论和虚假信息的信仰在

sentences.en: changed over the last 30 or 40 years, going back well before social media existed.
sentences.zh: 过去30或40年里是如何变化的，时间甚至可以追溯到社交媒体存在之前很久。

sentences.en: And it turns out that the rate of beliefs in conspiracy theories has been roughly constant over the last 40 years.
sentences.zh: 结果表明，过去40年来，对阴谋论深信不疑的比率大致保持不变。

sentences.en: It's just that some conspiracy theories have fallen out of fashion and other conspiracy theories have taken their place.
sentences.zh: 只是某些阴谋论已经过时，而其他阴谋论取而代之罢了。

sentences.en: We have this sense that social media is the driver of all of this fake information being spread around.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种感觉，认为社交媒体是所有这些虚假信息四处传播的幕后推手。

sentences.en: But I think if that was the case, you would see a sharp rise in the overall beliefs in conspiracy theories over the last 10 years or so.
sentences.zh: 但我认为如果是这样的话，你会看到在过去10年左右的时间里，人们对阴谋论的总体信仰急剧上升。

sentences.en: And that just doesn't seem to be the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk for a minute about your previous book, which was about inequality and how inequality affects how people think and behave.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们花一分钟聊聊你之前的书，那本书是关于不平等以及不平等如何影响人们的思维和行为的。

sentences.en: What's the role of inequality in driving polarization?
sentences.zh: 不平等在推动两极分化中扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: One of the effects of inequality increasing over the last 30 years is that there have always been the
sentences.zh: 过去30年不平等加剧的影响之一是，社会中一直都有

sentences.en: rich and the poor, but the rich and the poor are so much further apart from each other today than they were 30 years ago, right?
sentences.zh: 富人和穷人，但今天的富人和穷人之间的差距比30年前要大得多，对吧？

sentences.en: So the richest five or 10 or 1% have drastically more money and wealth than they did in the seventies or even the eighties.
sentences.zh: 因此，最富有的5%、10%或1%的人拥有的金钱和财富比七十年代甚至八十年代时有了惊人的增长。

sentences.en: And the coming apart of the relatively rich and the relatively poor has a number of consequences.
sentences.zh: 相对富裕阶层和相对贫困阶层的割裂带来了一系列后果。

sentences.en: They're social and health related, but also political.
sentences.zh: 它们与社交和健康有关，但也与政治有关。

sentences.en: And the chief effect that I think we see in terms of American politics is that when people find themselves either on a higher rung or a bottom rung of the socioeconomic ladder,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在美国政治中看到的主要影响是，当人们发现自己处于社会经济阶梯的较高阶层或最底层时，

sentences.en: they tend to justify and rationalize why it is that they're there, right?
sentences.zh: 他们往往会为自己为什么会呆在那里进行辩护和合理化解释，对吧？

sentences.en: So we've done studies, for example, that if we give people feedback that they have more money and wealth than other people they know, and we ask them why that might be.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做过研究，例如，如果我们给人们反馈，告诉他们自己比认识的其他人拥有更多的金钱和财富，并问他们这可能是为什么。

sentences.en: So this is not necessarily people who actually do have more money, but we're giving them a randomized feedback in a study.
sentences.zh: 所以这不一定是指那些实际拥有更多金钱的人，而是我们在研究中给他们提供了一个随机的反馈。

sentences.en: The typical response is to say, well, I worked hard and I earned that money.
sentences.zh: 典型的反应会说，嗯，我努力工作了，所以我赚到了这些钱。

sentences.en: If we take identical group of people and tell them you have less money or less wealth than people like you, why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 如果我们找来一组完全相同的人，并告诉他们你比像你这样的人拥有的金钱或财富更少，你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: They look at the exact same situation and say, well, it's because the system is unfair and I was disadvantaged by the following rigged system.
sentences.zh: 他们看着完全相同的情况会说，嗯，这是因为体制不公平，以下这个被操纵的体制让我处于不利地位。

sentences.en: And so people who end up on the top or the bottom of the economic ladder don't tend to attribute it to the luck of the draw or accidents of history.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些最终处于经济阶梯顶端或底端的人，往往不会将其归咎于运气的捉弄或历史的偶然。

sentences.en: They tend to think I'm a good and reasonable person.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会认为我是一个善良且讲道理的人。

sentences.en: So here's how I must have gotten here, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我是这样来到这里的，对吧？

sentences.en: And fill in those blanks with various justifications and rationalizations.
sentences.zh: 并用各种辩护和合理化解释来填补这些空白。

sentences.en: So one of the consequences of that is that when people either feel richer than others or are actually richer than others, they tend to think they earned
sentences.zh: 因此，其中一个后果是，当人们觉得自己比别人更有钱或者实际上比别人更有钱时，他们往往会认为这是自己

sentences.en: it and they tend to oppose redistributive policies and policies meant to help the poor because they think, well, I earned this through hard work and so can other people.
sentences.zh: 应得的，并且往往会反对再分配政策以及旨在帮助穷人的政策，因为他们认为，嗯，我是通过努力工作赚到这些钱的，其他人也可以。

sentences.en: Whereas when people occupy lower socioeconomic rungs, they tend to think, well, the system is broken and it's creating disadvantages for me.
sentences.zh: 而当人们处于较低的社会经济阶梯时，他们往往会认为，嗯，这个体制崩溃了，它正在给我带来不利地位。

sentences.en: So in that way, the rationalizations people come up with for their own economic status feed into what we believe about political groups and political policies.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，人们为自己的经济状况提出的合理化解释，助长了我们对政治团体和政治政策的信仰。

sentences.en: And as inequality arises and the richest 10% get further and further from the poorest 10%, that just exacerbates those political differences that go along with income inequality.
sentences.zh: 随着不平等的出现，最富有的10%与最贫困的10%之间的差距越来越大，这只会加剧伴随收入不平等而来的政治分歧。

sentences.en: I thought it was really interesting that you talk to people with, in some cases, a lot of money and that they were still, they had a sense that they weren't really rich.
sentences.zh: 我觉得非常有趣的是，你采访了一些在某些情况下拥有很多钱的人，他们仍然有一种自己其实并不算富有的感觉。

sentences.en: They didn't really have quite enough that there was this sense of dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上并没有足够的钱，有一种不满足感。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, does that conflict with the work of say, Dan Gilbert, who found that if you make about 70 odd thousand
sentences.zh: 我想知道，这是否与丹·吉尔伯特等人的研究相冲突？他们发现如果你每年赚大约七万

sentences.en: dollars a year, you don't get any happier than if you make a million dollars a year?
sentences.zh: 美元左右，你并不会比每年赚一百万美元感到更快乐？

sentences.en: So money makes a difference up to a certain point, like you said, and in that research a few years ago, it was somewhere around 70,000.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，金钱在达到一定程度之前会起作用，几年前的那项研究显示这个数字在大约七万左右。

sentences.en: Maybe it would be a bit higher today.
sentences.zh: 也许今天会稍微高一点。

sentences.en: But yeah, there's this diminishing marginal return when you look at the relationship between money and happiness.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，当你审视金钱与幸福之间的关系时，存在这种边际收益递减的规律。

sentences.en: And I think it's actually consistent with the idea that people adapt to where they are and start and keep comparing upward to those who have more.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这实际上与这样一种观点相吻合，即人们会适应他们所处的环境，并开始并不断向上与那些拥有更多的人进行比较。

sentences.en: So at some point, more money doesn't bring more happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，更多的钱并不能带来更多的幸福。

sentences.en: And I think that's in part because once you've got, say, $200,000 a year, and you're well above that threshold
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因是一旦你比如说每年有20万美元的收入，并且你远远超过了那个

sentences.en: for increased happiness, you're comparing yourself not to people who make $60,000 anymore.
sentences.zh: 增加幸福感的门槛，你就不再把自己与年收入6万美元的人进行比较了。

sentences.en: Now you're comparing to people who make $500,000.
sentences.zh: 现在你是在与年收入50万美元的人进行比较。

sentences.en: And so there's this shifting upward comparison that happens as people make more money.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着人们赚到更多的钱，会发生这种向上的比较转移。

sentences.en: And it's this fascinating, subjective squishiness that comes along with the idea of having enough.
sentences.zh: 这就是伴随着“拥有足够”这一概念而产生的一种迷人的、主观的模糊性。

sentences.en: It's a constantly moving target.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不断移动的目标。

sentences.en: Going back to the issue of polarization, do you have any advice or thoughts based on the work that you've done on how people can bridge the gap?
sentences.zh: 回到两极分化的议题上，基于你所做的工作，对于人们如何弥合分歧，你有什么建议或想法吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's a difficult question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个难题。

sentences.en: And I won't pretend to have easy answers to difficult questions.
sentences.zh: 我不会假装对难题有简单的答案。

sentences.en: But here's what I think the research suggests.
sentences.zh: 但这就是我认为研究给出的启示。

sentences.en: If we understand polarization as having to do with our social identities, and we understand that what people on
sentences.zh: 如果我们把两极分化理解为与我们的社会认同有关，并且我们理解

sentences.en: both sides of the aisle are doing is trying to make sense of what my status is in society,
sentences.zh: 政治光谱两边的人们正在做的事情，是试图弄清楚我在社会中的地位是什么，

sentences.en: and the social groups I belong to, and reassuring ourselves that we're good and reasonable people, and good members of our groups.
sentences.zh: 以及我所属的社会群体是什么，并向我们自己保证我们是善良且通情达理的人，是我们群体中的优秀成员。

sentences.en: When we're tempted to get into an argument with your relative on Facebook, or at the Thanksgiving dinner, et cetera, I think it helps to step away from just trying to prove them
sentences.zh: 当我们经受诱惑，想要在Facebook上或在感恩节晚宴等场合与你的亲戚争吵时，我认为抽身出来会有所帮助，不要试图去证明他们

sentences.en: wrong in terms of whatever argument they're making, or whatever ideas they're sharing.
sentences.zh: 无论提出什么论点或分享什么观点都是错的。

sentences.en: And to ask the question, what are they trying to do here?
sentences.zh: 而是去问这样一个问题，他们在这里试图做什么？

sentences.en: How are they using politics, or how are they using this argument to try to reassure themselves that they're a good and valuable person?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何利用政治，或者他们是如何利用这个论点来试图向自己保证他们是一个善良且有价值的人？

sentences.en: And then take a step back and say, maybe I'm doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 然后退一步说，也许我也在做同样的事情。

sentences.en: How am I using this argument to defend my sense that I'm a good and reasonable person?
sentences.zh: 我是如何利用这个论点来捍卫我“是一个善良且通情达理的人”这一自我感知的？

sentences.en: And it's not necessarily going to change either person's ideas about the political issue.
sentences.zh: 这不一定会改变任何一方对政治议题的看法。

sentences.en: But once you start interpreting that interaction, as two people doing the best they can
sentences.zh: 但一旦你开始将这种互动解释为两个人正在尽其所能

sentences.en: to reassure themselves that they're good and reasonable people, it's a very different conversation than if you're just focused narrowly on the political outrage of the moment.
sentences.zh: 来向自己保证他们是善良且通情达理的人，这就会是一场非常不同的对话，而不只是狭隘地专注于当下的政治愤怒。

sentences.en: So last question, what's next for you on the research front?
sentences.zh: 所以最后一个问题，你在研究方面下一步要做什么？

sentences.en: Are you, you have a new book percolating up there in your brain?
sentences.zh: 你、你的大脑里是不是正在酝酿一本新书？

sentences.en: No new book on the horizon yet.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有新书在筹备中。

sentences.en: Focused on this one at the moment.
sentences.zh: 目前专注于这一本。

sentences.en: But I'm really interested in understanding how these larger scale historical forces, like the ones we were talking about,
sentences.zh: 但我真的很有兴趣去了解这些更大规模的历史力量，比如我们一直在谈论的那些，

sentences.en: whether it's related to slavery and reconstruction, or later century, the Great Migration and other kinds
sentences.zh: 无论是与奴隶制和重建有关，还是后来的世纪、大迁徙以及其他各种

sentences.en: of demographic and cultural and historical changes have set the stage for a lot of the psychological processes that we see going on now.
sentences.zh: 人口统计学、文化和历史变革，是如何为我们现在看到的许多心理过程奠定基础的。

sentences.en: So that relationship between history and sometimes very ancient history and current day psychology is what I'm really focused on right now.
sentences.zh: 因此，历史——有时是非常古代的历史——与当代心理学之间的这种关系，正是我现在真正关注的重点。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Payne, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 佩恩博士，我想感谢你今天能来参加。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure talking with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能与你交谈。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org, or on Apple, Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 上找到《心理学说话》往期的节目，也可以在苹果、Spotify、YouTube 或任何您收听播客的地方找到。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please subscribe and leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢听到的内容，请订阅并给我们留下评价。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学说话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学协会的基姆·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。
